preview.content:
[Build Blueprint]
Section | Decision | Notes
Hero | Browser-based voxel sandbox | A playable Minecraft-style prototype focused on movement, block placement, block removal, and terrain.
01 Core Loop | Explore, mine, place, repeat | The first version should feel tactile before it feels huge.
02 Rendering | Three.js voxel world | Use instanced meshes for block performance instead of one mesh per cube.
03 Terrain | Chunked procedural terrain | Generate small chunks around the player using seeded noise.
04 Controls | Pointer lock first-person movement | WASD, mouse look, jump, sprint, left-click remove, right-click place.
05 Blocks | Starter palette | Grass, dirt, stone, wood, leaves, sand, water placeholder, glass placeholder.
06 Inventory | Hotbar first | Nine slots, scroll wheel selection, number-key shortcuts.
07 Persistence | Local save | Store edited blocks in browser localStorage or IndexedDB.
08 Polish | Small signals matter | Block outline, footstep bob, placement sound, simple sky, fog, day tint.

[MVP Scope]
Feature | Priority | Acceptance Criteria
First-person camera | P0 | Mouse look works smoothly after pointer lock.
Player movement | P0 | WASD movement, gravity, jumping, and collision against blocks.
Voxel terrain | P0 | World loads with varied height terrain and visible block types.
Block removal | P0 | Targeted block disappears with left click.
Block placement | P0 | Selected block appears on targeted face with right click.
Hotbar | P1 | Nine slots render on screen and selection changes with keys or wheel.
Chunk loading | P1 | Nearby chunks load without freezing the browser.
Save edits | P1 | Placed and removed blocks persist after reload.
Lighting | P2 | Basic directional light and ambient fill give readable depth.
Mobile support | P3 | Deferred; first build should prioritize desktop playability.

[Technical Plan]
Layer | Recommended Approach | Reason
App shell | Vite + TypeScript | Fast local iteration and clean browser build pipeline.
3D engine | Three.js | Reliable WebGL abstraction with broad examples and ecosystem support.
Physics | Simple AABB collision | Enough for voxel walking without pulling in a heavy engine.
Terrain noise | Simplex or Perlin noise | Creates natural hills and variation with minimal data.
Chunk size | 16 x 16 x 64 | Small enough for fast rebuilds, familiar enough for voxel conventions.
Mesh strategy | Greedy meshing or instanced meshes | Avoids rendering every hidden cube face.
State model | Chunk map plus edit overlay | Procedural base terrain stays cheap; player edits stay explicit.
Storage | IndexedDB for larger saves | More durable than localStorage once worlds grow.
Assets | Texture atlas | One material pass, cleaner block rendering, easier expansion.

[Implementation Phases]
Phase | Output | Definition of Done
1 | Scene foundation | Canvas renders sky, light, camera, and a flat test block field.
2 | Player controller | Player can walk, jump, collide, and look around without falling through terrain.
3 | Procedural terrain | Chunks generate around spawn with grass, dirt, and stone layers.
4 | Raycast editing | Player can aim at blocks, remove them, and place selected blocks.
5 | Hotbar UI | Selection is visible, responsive, and mapped to block types.
6 | Persistence | World edits survive reload.
7 | Performance pass | Hidden faces are reduced and movement stays smooth on normal desktop hardware.
8 | Feel pass | Block outline, sounds, fog, and subtle camera polish make it feel like a real sandbox.

[Risks]
Risk | Impact | Mitigation
Too many meshes | Frame rate collapses | Use instancing, face culling, or greedy meshing early.
Collision bugs | Player clips through world | Keep physics simple and test against stairs, edges, and tunnels.
Chunk rebuild spikes | Stutter while editing | Rebuild only affected chunk and neighboring border when needed.
Browser memory growth | Long sessions degrade | Unload distant chunks and cap active radius.
Scope creep | Prototype becomes unfinished | Ship core loop before mobs, crafting, caves, multiplayer, or advanced lighting.
Texture mismatch | World feels cheap | Use a consistent low-res atlas instead of mixed placeholder colors.

[Next Build Target]
Target | Concrete Spec
Playable prototype | A desktop browser Minecraft-style sandbox with first-person movement, procedural chunks, block breaking, block placing, and a nine-slot hotbar.
Recommended first milestone | One HTML app running locally with Three.js, generated terrain, raycast block editing, and no backend.
What to skip first | Crafting, enemies, multiplayer, infinite caves, complex water, redstone-style logic, account systems.
Sharp editor note | The clone does not need a massive world on day one. It needs one block under the cursor that feels correct when it breaks.
